title: Apparatus for Harvesting Tissue Microcolumns
protocol: Secure a female luer lock connector onto a post.
Mount the post perpendicularly onto a second horizontal rotation stage.
Position this first rotation stage vertically and mount it onto a two-axis translation stage.
Fasten the combination of stages onto a stable surface, such as an optical breadboard.
Separately mount a rotary tool onto the same breadboard at approximately the same height as the luer lock connector.
Install two cut-off wheels concentrically onto the rotary tool, with a smaller lower grit diamond cut-off wheel over a larger higher grit stone cut-off wheel.
Position an overhead light source with an adjustable arm over the rotary tool aimed at the cutting wheels.
Position a dissecting microscope over the production setup so that the eyepiece is focused on the cutting discs.
Wear protective eyewear and a surgical mask.
Choose hypodermic needles based on experimental requirements.
Mark off the intended length on each harvesting needle.
Lower the needle perpendicularly to the rotary tool with power on, using the edge of the outer cutting disc to cut off excess length at the marked point.
Connect the shortened, blunt needle to the female luer lock connector on the production stage.
Adjust the horizontal rotation stage so that the needle is at a 12° angle parallel to the cutting discs.
Turn on the overhead light and adjust its position while observing the needle under magnification until the light reflects off the midline of the needle.
Power on the rotary tool, then use the translation stage to advance the needle towards the inner (diamond) cutting disc.
Advance the needle slowly against the cutting disc until reaching approximately the midline of the needle as visualized by overhead light reflection.
Move the cut needle surface from the inner diamond wheel onto the outer stone wheel for finer polish.
Retract the needle away from the cutting disc.
Rotate the needle 180° using the vertical rotation stage.
Repeat steps to reshape the other side of the needle until it has two cutting tips of approximately equal length.
Clean the inside bore with a metal wire slightly smaller than the needle's inner diameter.
Use a sharp wooden stick to remove any burrs from the edges of the newly-formed needle.
Administer local lidocaine and epinephrine by intradermal injection for analgesia and to reduce bleeding in live animals.
Fill a standard syringe with normal saline and connect it to a harvesting needle.
Completely insert the harvesting needle into the donor skin, then retract it.
Push on the piston of the syringe to flush saline through the harvesting needle and expel the microcolumn that is lodged in the needle bore.
Repeat steps 2.4.2 and 2.4.3 3 to 5 times before expelling the microcolumns.
Expel the microcolumns into a standard cell strainer for ease of collection.
Increase pressure on the piston if needles become clogged to clear the stuck tissue.
Insert a metal wire through the needle tip opening to clear any remaining clogs in the needle bore.
Keep the microcolumns submerged in saline or medium until use to prevent desiccation.
Create a simple suction-assisted device for collecting large amounts of microcolumns.
Remove the plunger from a 20 mL syringe.
Attach the syringe to a suction adapter typically used for liposuction.
Connect a harvesting needle to the assembled syringe.
Use sterile suction tubing to connect the suction adapter to a sterile suction canister.
Ensure the harvesting apparatus is connected to a canister input allowing fluid to flow into the canister unimpeded.
Connect the apparatus to a negative pressure source.
Insert the harvesting needle into the skin to harvest microcolumns.
Flush the system intermittently with sterile saline during the procedure.
